clue.text: Coming from abroad, one left on board falls in sea

indicators.note: what falls in something ends up inside it, so one piece drops into the other

parts.note: port is the left side aboard a ship

explanation.surface: A sailor from overseas tumbles off the left side of the ship into the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' reads as a sailor's position; port is the nautical word for the left-hand side of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Imported goods are brought in from another country, so they are coming from abroad.

clue.text: Animal is tangled up in large piece of canvas

indicators.note: things tangled up are jumbled out of their proper order, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A creature has got itself caught up in a big sheet of canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: The mainsail is the principal sail of a ship, a large sheet of canvas.

clue.text: Resisting enlightenment, having messed up subtractions

indicators.note: sums that are messed up have their parts in the wrong places, so the letters get rearranged

explanation.surface: A pupil who has got their take-away sums wrong is accused of refusing to learn.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscurantist describes opposing the spread of knowledge, deliberately keeping things obscure.

clue.text: Name Gray had for Welsh poet

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the first name of the poet Gray, author of the Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard
second meaning: the surname of Dylan, who wrote Under Milk Wood

explanation.walkthrough: One poet's first name is another poet's surname: Thomas Gray, the English poet, and Dylan Thomas, the Welsh one.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas was Gray's given name, and it is the family name of the twentieth-century Welsh writer Dylan.

clue.text: May first, for example, become old-fashioned

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a particular day of the calendar
second meaning: to go out of style, as a fashion does over time

explanation.walkthrough: 'May' looks like a modal verb opening a sentence; it is the month.
explanation.definitionFit: The first of May is a calendar day, and things that date grow stale and look of their period.

clue.text: Disconnected way to play toccatas in new arrangement

indicators.note: a piece put in a new arrangement has its parts reordered, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A musician tries playing toccatas choppily in a fresh version.
explanation.definitionFit: Staccato is the musical direction for notes played short and detached from each other.

clue.text: Graves found in cellar, say

parts.note: surface reading: tombs discovered in a basement, a grisly find
setter's reading: Graves is a Bordeaux district and the drink named after it, the sort of bottle kept in a cellar

explanation.walkthrough: The capital G is hidden by its place at the start of the clue; Graves is the Bordeaux region, and 'say' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Graves is a red or white Bordeaux, one example of the drink stored in cellars.

clue.text: Part of French capital deposited with moneylender

parts.note: something deposited has been left somewhere

explanation.surface: Some French capital, meaning money, has been put into a lending house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French capital' reads as euros or francs; it is Paris, whose south bank of the Seine is the Left Bank.
explanation.definitionFit: The Left Bank is the southern district of Paris along the Seine, famous for artists and students.

clue.text: Trick requiring skill if leading diamonds

indicators.note: what is leading goes in front, so these pieces come before the last one

explanation.surface: A card trick needs dexterity when diamonds are led.
explanation.definitionFit: An artifice is a clever device or stratagem used to deceive, a trick.

clue.text: Cut initial sources of needles

indicators.note: something cut is shortened, here by losing its final letter

parts.note: the initial thing is the first

explanation.surface: Trim the first needles taken from a source, as a sewing or pine instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: FIRST loses its tail to leave the trees. 'Initial' wants to signal first letters, but it is the word being cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Fir trees are conifers that grow and shed needle-shaped leaves.

clue.text: Start business with 1000 workers and stick together

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
to cement is to bind firmly

explanation.surface: Launch a firm with a thousand staff who are united.
explanation.definitionFit: A commencement is a beginning, the moment something starts.

clue.text: Models act as crew that's needed for shooting

definitions.note: read as 'what is needed for shooting'

parts.note: a car or weapon model is a mark, as in Mark II
to act as crew is to man a ship

explanation.surface: Fashion models serve as a film crew on a photo shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shooting' looks like a photo or film shoot with models; it is firing at targets.
explanation.definitionFit: Marksmanship is skill at hitting a target, the ability good shooting requires.

clue.text: A pass from wing in the French game

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside it

parts.note: A, plus a cross, a football pass played in from the wing

explanation.surface: A winger's pass in a French football match.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrosse is a team sport played with netted sticks, originally North American.

clue.text: Legally remove some of the victims

indicators.note: only a portion of the following words is used, a run of letters within them

parts.note: the run straddles the two words

explanation.surface: A court lawfully throws out several of those who suffered.
explanation.definitionFit: To evict is to expel a tenant from property through the legal process.

clue.text: If a car is going astray, it has a horn

indicators.note: something going astray wanders off its proper course, so the letters wander out of order

explanation.surface: A wayward car at least has a horn to warn people.
explanation.walkthrough: The car's horn is a hooter; the definition means the Horn of Africa, the continent's eastern peninsula.
explanation.definitionFit: The Horn of Africa is the peninsula jutting into the Arabian Sea, so the continent has a horn.

clue.text: Design section of aeroplane near rear

indicators.note: a section is only a part of the whole, a run of consecutive letters
says the part sits towards the back end of the word that holds it

parts.note: the run lies towards the end of the word

explanation.surface: Engineers draw up a section of an aircraft towards its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan is a drawing or scheme for how something is to be built or done, a design.

clue.text: Job English medic set up that helps with deliveries

definitions.note: read as 'something that helps with deliveries'

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means raised so the letters read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A British doctor arranges a post that helps when babies are delivered.
explanation.walkthrough: A medic and deliveries suggest childbirth; the deliveries are of mail.
explanation.definitionFit: A postcode is the alphanumeric address code that lets mail be sorted and delivered.

clue.text: Go after one European friend or another

definitions.note: another friend from Europe, the Spanish one

indicators.note: placing a piece after another means it comes later in the answer

parts.note: ami is the French word for a friend

explanation.surface: Pick one friend from Europe to accompany you, or a different one.
explanation.walkthrough: The French friend plus GO gives the Spanish friend, hence 'another'.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for friend, so it is a second European word for a pal after the French one.

clue.text: Like office trainees, perhaps, object over board's conclusion

parts.note: an article is an object or item

indicators.note: a conclusion is an end, so only the final letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: Junior staff object when the boardroom meeting wraps up.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'over' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: An articled clerk is bound by a training contract to a solicitor, so trainees in a law office may be articled.

clue.text: Belt, or other article of clothing or clobber

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to punch someone hard
second meaning: something worn on the foot, a garment other than a belt
third meaning: to hit, again a blow

explanation.walkthrough: 'Belt' and 'clobber' both look like clothing (clobber is British slang for clothes), but they mean hit; 'other' marks the true garment.
explanation.definitionFit: To sock someone is to strike them, and a sock is also a garment worn on the foot.

clue.text: Island restricted by absurdly erratic standards

indicators.note: one thing restricted by others is hemmed in by them, so it goes inside
something done absurdly makes no sense, so the letters are thrown into nonsense order

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: An island community is hemmed in by some ridiculously inconsistent rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Criteria are the benchmarks by which something is judged, the standards applied.

clue.text: Went off, upset about nothing

indicators.note: one thing about another goes around it, enclosing it

explanation.surface: Someone stormed out, distressed over a trifle.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has spoilt has gone bad, which is what 'went off' means of milk or meat.

clue.text: Isolated state of Australians felt, ultimately, as madness

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the preceding word counts

explanation.surface: Australians felt that remote life drove them mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Isolated state' sounds like a mood the Australians feel; it is the island state cut off from the mainland.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasmania is the Australian state on an island separated from the mainland by Bass Strait.

clue.text: Follow performance with commercial break?

indicators.note: a break interrupts something, so one piece sits in the middle of the other

parts.note: a TV commercial is an ad

explanation.surface: A viewer asks whether to keep watching a TV show that has an advert break.
explanation.definitionFit: To shadow someone is to follow them closely, often secretly.

clue.text: Finding fault with service, enough to produce reaction

parts.note: the Mass is a church service

explanation.surface: A churchgoer complains about the service enough to provoke a response.
explanation.definitionFit: Critical mass is the minimum quantity of fissile material needed to sustain a chain reaction.

clue.text: Part of poetic line — the writer is British

parts.note: the writer refers to himself: I am

explanation.surface: A poet announces their nationality in a line of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The writer' is the setter speaking of themselves, so 'the writer is' becomes I AM.
explanation.definitionFit: An iamb is a metrical foot of one unstressed and one stressed syllable, a unit of a verse line.

clue.text: Ruler producing line on circle — radius, then diameter

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line
the letter O is round like a circle
R is the abbreviation for radius
D is the abbreviation for diameter

explanation.surface: A ruler used to draw a line, a circle, its radius and diameter, like a geometry lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruler' looks like the drawing instrument suited to the geometry; it means a sovereign.
explanation.definitionFit: A lord is a master or sovereign, someone who rules over others.

clue.text: What's writ large for either Aphrodite or Artemis, or another Greek goddess

parts.note: the pronoun standing for either goddess; that the answer also runs through 'either Aphrodite' is a coincidence
the capital letter at the start of both names

explanation.surface: Puzzling over what is emphasised for two goddesses, or for a third.
explanation.walkthrough: Both Aphrodite and Artemis begin with a capital A, so the letter writ large for either is her A.
explanation.definitionFit: Hera was queen of the Olympian gods, wife of Zeus, a Greek goddess besides the two named.

clue.text: Behave imperiously as person who's active around pit

indicators.note: one thing around another surrounds it, holding it inside

parts.note: a doer is an active person
a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: A busy pit boss lords it over the miners.
explanation.definitionFit: To domineer is to assert one's will over others in an overbearing, arrogant way.

clue.text: Make little of sad tragedy, for instance

parts.note: a tragedy is one kind of play

explanation.surface: Someone minimises a sorrowful disaster as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: To downplay something is to make it seem less important than it is, to minimise it.
